name: Question 1
problem: A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin $O$ with acceleration, measured in $\text{m}/{\text{s}}^{2},$ given by the function $a(t)=-\frac{4}{(2+t)^{2}}$, where $t$ is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity $v=2\,\text{m}/\text{s}$ when $t=0\,\text{s}$, find the velocity (in $\text{m}/\text{s}$) of the particle at time $t.$

Question 1
?

A particle moves along a straight line relative to a fixed origin O with acceleration, measured in m/s2, given by the function a(t)=−4(2+t)2, where t is the time in seconds. If the particle has velocity v=2m/s when t=0s, find the velocity (in m/s) of the particle at time t.

a
 v(t)=42+t
b
 v(t)=22+t+1
c
 v(t)=16(2+t)3
d
 v(t)=8(2+t)3+1
e
 v(t)=42+t+2
